content: Two viable strategies for adding a synthetic item to a virtualized feed: (A) index/offset trickery such as the 'firstItemIndex' pattern (start indices at a large synthetic offset, decrement to prepend) used by virtuoso-style virtualizers to insert without shifting visible content -- only works if you own the virtualizer. (B) For feeds you do NOT own (X's own virtualizer), the robust approach is to splice a synthetic entry into the underlying data response before the owning app's virtualizer ever sees it (e.g. intercept the timeline GraphQL/XHR response in the page's JS context and insert a fake 'entry' matching the shape of a real one), letting X's own code render it exactly like a real tweet -- this avoids all DOM-fighting since you never touch React-owned nodes. Raw DOM sibling insertion into an already-mounted virtualized list is fragile: cells are usually absolutely positioned via computed transform:translateY(px) offsets keyed to index count, so an injected sibling either overlaps existing cells or gets wiped on the next re-render/recycle pass. Node-processed tracking commonly uses a WeakSet keyed on the DOM element (auto-GC's when the node is discarded) or a data-* marker attribute (survives serialization/HTML diffing tools) checked before decorating, to avoid double-injecting into recycled nodes.
